Hi Product Hunt, I'm Emad, one of the makers of Octri. 👋  
  
If you ship an API you know the routine: write the docs by hand, bolt on an SDK generator, then have no idea when those SDKs break inside someone's production app. Octri does the whole thing from one OpenAPI spec: a docs site, SDKs in ten languages (TypeScript, Python, Go, Rust, Ruby, PHP, Java, Kotlin, Swift, Dart) and an MCP server so Claude or Cursor can call your API.  
  
What is new though? Let me tell you! The SDKs monitor themselves. A failed call in a user's app comes back as a de-minified stack trace tagged to the exact release. No separate error-tracking setup! more about how it works and its security here: [...] GitHub sync regenerates and republishes everything on every merge. results.title: Press kit | Octri
results.content:
Octri is a platform for teams that publish an API. It takes an OpenAPI specification and produces four things from it: a documentation site, client SDKs in ten languages (TypeScript, Python, Go, Rust, Ruby, PHP, Dart, Swift, Java and Kotlin), an MCP server so AI agents can call the API, and monitoring that reports errors from inside those SDKs once they are running in customers’ applications. The monitoring is the part nothing else does. A generated client runs in a process its author has no access to, so when it mishandles a response the failure never reaches the API provider’s logs: the request succeeded. Octri reports those failures from inside the client, paired to the release that produced them, so a broken SDK is something a team finds rather than something a customer reports. [...] 90 words
